subject: POC prompt dataset collection - AcmeCorp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC follow-up — prompt set & eval dataset (next steps)

Hi Alex / Tara —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about AcmeCorp's use case for customer support summarization and action-item extraction. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can move the POC forward: 

Recap (what I heard):
- Goal: reduce average time-to-resolution by surfacing suggested next steps and summaries in agent UI.
- Success criteria: 1) 15% reduction in agent handle time for tickets in scope, 2) >= 90% precision on suggested action-items in a human review sample, 3) no PII leakage in generated outputs.
- Initial scope: 2 teams, ~1,500 weekly tickets, English only.

Proposed POC plan (short):
1) You share a prompt set + representative examples (500-1,000 prompts / ticket excerpts) and 1 week of anonymized system logs for model compatibility checks.
2) We run an internal eval to produce baseline metrics (latency, token cost, precision/recall) and surface failure modes.
3) Joint evaluation: we run the eval harness on a held-out set and review results in a 60-90 minute session.
4) Iterate on prompts and routing/quantization recommendations; final sign-off on success criteria.

Ownership / timelines:
- Acme: provide prompt set + sample logs by end of week (Fri 7/16). Attachments accepted as CSV/JSON.
- Redwood (Marissa + Dev): run eval and share initial results by 7/21.

Action items for Acme: please provide:
- A CSV of prompts / ticket excerpts (columns: ticket_id, prompt_text, expected_action_items [optional], class_label) - anonymized.
- One-week sample of system logs (redacted) or a small archive with examples of long contexts that matter for latency.
- Any regulatory constraints or redaction rules we should apply.

We can accept files via the shared Drive link (below) or SFTP if you prefer. I've attached a lightweight template (acmecorp_prompts_template.csv) to make formatting easier - if you already have something similar, feel free to send it as-is.

Related links: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/POC-452

If this plan looks good, reply with who on your side will own the data drop and whether you prefer Drive or SFTP. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the template.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: acmecorp_prompts_template.csv (CSV template for prompts)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the plan and timeline from our side. A couple of clarifications: 

- For the "expected_action_items" column, is free-text OK or do you prefer a set of tags? We can provide both but want to keep the CSV size small.
- For the system logs: we have a redaction pipeline. We'll provide a redacted week and a mapping doc for any substitutions we make.

Ownership: I'll own the data handoff and Tara will coordinate with our security team on the redaction. We'll upload to the Drive link by EOD Fri 7/16.

One more ask - can you confirm whether Redwood needs the original ticket context length (full conversation) or just the last 1-2 messages? Some tickets have very long threads and we'd rather not include whole transcripts if shorter context is sufficient.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex —

Short answers to your questions: 
- expected_action_items: free-text is fine; having an optional tag column helps our automated scorers but isn't required. If you can provide a small mapping of common tags (e.g., refund, escalate, follow-up), that speeds iteration.
- Context length: please include the last 1-2 messages plus any system metadata (ticket type, priority). For 1-2 very large threads we can take full transcripts as samples, but start with shorter excerpts to keep dataset size manageable.

Also attaching a short eval plan (bulleted) below - we'll fill in the exact metrics after we ingest your files: 

Eval plan (high level):
- Ingest your prompt set and split into training / holdout (we ask for 80/20 split if possible).
- Run Redwood eval harness to measure: precision/recall on action-item extraction, summarization ROUGE/F1 vs human labels, token latency and cost per request, and PII leakage checks.
- Share initial dashboard and a list of top 10 failure cases.

We will also surface model variant recommendations (quantized vs full precision) and batching profiles that meet your latency SLO.

Next steps: once you upload the files we will: 1) ingest and run preflight checks (24-48 hrs), 2) share initial results by 7/21, 3) schedule the joint review on 7/22 or 7/23.

Thanks - looking forward to the dataset.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Product Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com

Attachment: acme_eval_plan_v1.md (short eval checklist)
